1.headline: Countries Talk About Rules for Killer Robots
p: Good morning. This is your morning news in English.
Can a machine decide to kill a person? Countries are talking about this now.

This week, many countries are meeting in Geneva. Geneva is a city in Switzerland. The meeting is backed by the United Nations. They are talking about new weapons. These weapons can attack without a person's choice. Some people call them killer robots.

A top United Nations leader asked for strong rules. He said humans must make these choices. About 130 countries want new rules. But every country must agree. The United States and Russia want fewer rules.
Why is this important? Drones are used in many wars today. Machines are getting smarter fast.
Again, countries are meeting to talk about rules for killer robots.
Thank you for listening.

According to news reports, a meeting backed by the United Nations opened on Monday in Geneva, Switzerland. Countries will decide whether to start talks on new rules for lethal autonomous weapons. These weapons can choose and attack targets without a human. Some people call them killer robots.

Why does it matter? Armed drones are used in wars today, like in Ukraine and the Middle East. As artificial intelligence gets better, these weapons may spread.
To sum up, countries are talking about rules for killer robots, but not everyone agrees.
Thank you for listening.

3.headline: Geneva Talks Weigh Rules for Weapons That Choose Their Own Targets
p: Good morning. This is your morning news in English.
Should a machine ever decide, on its own, to kill a person? This week, countries are meeting to talk about that question.

According to the Associated Press, a United Nations-backed conference opened on Monday in Geneva, Switzerland. It is a review meeting of a treaty called the Convention on Certain Conventional Weapons. A treaty is an agreement between countries. Delegates will decide whether to start talks on new rules for lethal autonomous weapons. These are weapons that can choose and attack targets without a human making the final decision. Some people call them killer robots.

Volker Türk, the United Nations human rights chief, urged countries to agree on binding rules quickly. Binding means the rules must be followed. He said the world faces important choices about the role of humans in war. The head of the International Committee of the Red Cross also said the future of war should not be handed over to machines.

Seven countries, including Austria, Brazil and Mexico, proposed negotiations last month. An advocacy group called Stop Killer Robots says about 130 countries support new rules. Decisions at this conference need consensus, which means every country must agree. Reports say the United States and Russia want to limit any rules on their weapons. Russia said it is too early for bans or limits.

Why does this matter? Armed drones are now common in wars, including in Ukraine and the Middle East. Activists say some drones have already struck targets on their own. As artificial intelligence improves, these weapons could spread quickly.
To sum up, countries are meeting in Geneva to discuss rules for weapons that can kill without human control, but some big military powers are not ready to agree.
Thank you for listening.

4.headline: Geneva Conference Weighs Talks on Lethal Autonomous Weapons
p: Good morning, and welcome to your morning news in English.
Who should have the final say over life and death on the battlefield: a soldier, or an algorithm? That question is at the center of a major meeting in Geneva this week.

Delegates have gathered at United Nations offices for the seventh review conference of the Convention on Certain Conventional Weapons, according to the Associated Press. Their task is to decide whether to launch formal negotiations on rules for lethal autonomous weapons, systems that can select and strike targets without direct human control. Critics often describe them as killer robots.

On Monday, U.N. human rights chief Volker Türk urged governments to agree urgently on binding limits, warning that the international community faces critical choices about the role of humans in decisions to use force. Days earlier, the president of the International Committee of the Red Cross said states must make sure the future of warfare is not handed over to machines. U.N. Secretary-General Antonio Guterres had set this year as a deadline for launching talks.

Momentum has been building. Last month, seven countries, including Austria, Brazil, Ireland and New Zealand, submitted a proposal for negotiations toward a legally binding agreement. The advocacy group Stop Killer Robots says some 130 countries back new international rules. However, the convention works by consensus, so a single country can block a deal. The United States and Russia are reported to be resisting tight restrictions, and Russia's Foreign Ministry said it was premature to talk about prohibitions.

The stakes are rising. Armed drones have become a defining feature of modern conflicts, from Ukraine to the Middle East, and activists say drones that can strike on their own have already been used in some cases. With artificial intelligence advancing rapidly, supporters of a treaty argue that rules are needed before such weapons spread widely.
To sum up, the Geneva talks could open the door to the first global rules on autonomous weapons, but resistance from major military powers may keep that door closed for now.
Thank you for listening.

5.headline: Geneva Weighs First Global Talks on 'Killer Robots' as Major Powers Hesitate
p: Good morning, and welcome to your morning news in English.
Should the decision to take a human life ever be delegated to a machine? That stark question is hanging over a pivotal round of diplomacy in Geneva this week.

Delegates have convened at United Nations offices for the seventh review conference of the Convention on Certain Conventional Weapons, the treaty framework that has previously restricted arms such as blinding lasers. According to the Associated Press, they must decide whether to open formal negotiations on lethal autonomous weapons systems, which can identify and engage targets without meaningful human intervention, and which campaigners have dubbed killer robots.

The calls for action have grown increasingly insistent. On Monday, U.N. human rights chief Volker Türk urged states to agree, as a matter of urgency, on binding limits, arguing that the choices made now will shape the future of armed conflict and the place of human judgment within it. The president of the International Committee of the Red Cross, Mirjana Spoljaric, likewise warned that warfare must not be handed over to machines, while Secretary-General Antonio Guterres has set this year as the deadline for launching talks.

On paper, the momentum is considerable. Last month, a cross-regional group of seven countries, among them Austria, Mexico and Panama, tabled a proposal for negotiations on a legally binding instrument, and the coalition Stop Killer Robots counts roughly 130 nations in favor of new rules. Yet the convention operates by consensus, effectively handing any single member a veto. Washington and Moscow are reported to be wary of curbs on their freedom to develop and field new technologies, and Russia's Foreign Ministry has dismissed talk of restrictions or bans as premature.

The backdrop lends the debate real urgency. Armed drones have become ubiquitous in conflicts from Ukraine to the Middle East, and activists say systems capable of striking independently have already been deployed in isolated cases, though not on a wide scale. As artificial intelligence reshapes the battlefield, treaty advocates contend that the window for setting guardrails is narrowing.
To sum up, Geneva could mark the start of the first global negotiations on autonomous weapons, but with consensus required and major powers dragging their feet, a breakthrough is far from guaranteed.
Thank you for listening.

제임스 본드는 영화 속 유명한 스파이입니다. 그의 번호는 007입니다. 패틴슨은 이 역할을 맡는 일곱 번째 배우입니다. 그 전에는 대니얼 크레이그가 본드를 연기했습니다.
많은 사람이 '트와일라잇' 영화로 패틴슨을 압니다. 그는 배트맨도 연기했습니다.
새 본드 영화는 아직 제목이 없습니다. 유명한 감독 드니 빌뇌브가 만듭니다. 그는 '듄' 영화들도 만들었습니다.
알고 계셨나요? 첫 번째 본드 영화는 1962년에 나왔습니다.
다시 말해, 로버트 패틴슨이 새 제임스 본드입니다.
들어 주셔서 감사합니다.

tr: 좋은 아침입니다. 아침 영어 뉴스입니다.

왜 재미있는 소식일까요? 많은 사람이 누가 본드를 연기해야 하는지에 대해 강한 의견을 가지고 있습니다. 이제 모두가 패틴슨에 대해 이야기할 수 있습니다.

3.headline: Robert Pattinson Named the Next James Bond
p: Good morning. This is your morning news in English.
The world finally knows who will be the next James Bond. It is British actor Robert Pattinson.

According to news reports, the James Bond film series announced the news on Monday. Pattinson, who is 40 years old, will become the seventh actor to play the famous spy, known as 007, in the official films. He follows Daniel Craig, who played Bond in five movies. Craig's last Bond film, No Time to Die, came out in 2021.

Pattinson first became famous as a teenage vampire in the Twilight movies. Later he took on more serious roles. He played Batman, and he is now working on another Batman film. He also stars in The Odyssey, a new film by director Christopher Nolan.

The new Bond movie does not have a title yet. It will be the 26th film in the series, and it will be directed by Denis Villeneuve, the director of the Dune movies. This is also the first Bond film made under the creative control of Amazon MGM Studios. Creative control means the power to make the big decisions about the story and the actors. Amazon took over after the longtime producers, Barbara Broccoli and Michael G. Wilson, left the series in 2025.
Did you know? The first James Bond film, Dr. No, came out in 1962. Since then, the series has earned more than seven billion dollars around the world.

To sum up, Robert Pattinson is the new James Bond, in a film directed by Denis Villeneuve.
Thank you for listening.
tr: 좋은 아침입니다. 아침 영어 뉴스입니다.

패틴슨은 처음에 '트와일라잇' 영화의 10대 뱀파이어로 유명해졌습니다. 이후 더 진지한 역할을 맡았습니다. 그는 배트맨을 연기했고, 지금은 또 다른 배트맨 영화를 작업하고 있습니다. 또한 크리스토퍼 놀런 감독의 새 영화 '오디세이'에도 출연합니다.

새 본드 영화는 아직 제목이 없습니다. 시리즈의 26번째 영화가 되며, '듄' 영화들의 감독인 드니 빌뇌브가 연출합니다. 또한 아마존 MGM 스튜디오가 창작 통제권을 가진 첫 본드 영화입니다. 창작 통제권이란 이야기와 배우에 관한 큰 결정을 내리는 권한을 뜻합니다. 아마존은 오랜 제작자인 바버라 브로콜리와 마이클 G. 윌슨이 2025년 시리즈를 떠난 뒤 이를 넘겨받았습니다.

정리하면, 로버트 패틴슨이 드니 빌뇌브 감독 영화의 새 제임스 본드입니다.
들어 주셔서 감사합니다.

4.headline: Robert Pattinson Cast as the Seventh James Bond
p: Good morning, and welcome to your morning news in English.

One of the longest-running guessing games in Hollywood is finally over: Robert Pattinson is the next James Bond. For months, fans and film critics had traded predictions about who would inherit the famous tuxedo.

The franchise announced on Monday that the 40-year-old British actor will take on the role of the world's most famous secret agent, according to news reports. Pattinson becomes the seventh actor to play 007 in the official film series, succeeding Daniel Craig, whose five-film run ended with No Time to Die in 2021.

The casting caps a remarkable career shift. Pattinson first rose to fame as a brooding vampire in the Twilight films before building a reputation for darker, more challenging roles. He took on the role of Batman and is currently in production on another Batman film, and he also appears in Christopher Nolan's The Odyssey.

The still-untitled movie will be the 26th Bond film, and it will be directed by Denis Villeneuve, the filmmaker behind the Dune series. It is also the first Bond production under the creative control of Amazon MGM Studios. Amazon took charge after Barbara Broccoli and Michael G. Wilson, whose family had guided the franchise for decades, stepped away in 2025.
Did you know? Since the first Bond movie in 1962, the series has earned more than seven billion dollars at the global box office, making it one of the most successful series in film history.

The decision matters well beyond fan debates. Bond is one of the most valuable properties in entertainment, and Amazon's first choice of lead actor offers a strong signal of how it plans to steer the franchise for years to come.
To sum up, Robert Pattinson will be the new 007 in a Denis Villeneuve film, the first Bond movie made under Amazon's control.
Thank you for listening.
tr: 좋은 아침입니다. 아침 영어 뉴스에 오신 것을 환영합니다.

보도에 따르면, 본드 프랜차이즈는 월요일 40세 영국 배우가 세계에서 가장 유명한 비밀 요원 역을 맡는다고 발표했습니다. 패틴슨은 공식 영화 시리즈에서 007을 연기하는 일곱 번째 배우가 되며, 2021년 '노 타임 투 다이'로 다섯 편의 출연을 마친 대니얼 크레이그의 뒤를 잇습니다.
이번 캐스팅은 놀라운 경력 변화의 정점입니다. 패틴슨은 '트와일라잇' 영화의 우수에 찬 뱀파이어로 처음 유명해진 뒤, 더 어둡고 도전적인 역할로 명성을 쌓았습니다. 그는 배트맨 역을 맡았고 현재 또 다른 배트맨 영화를 촬영 중이며, 크리스토퍼 놀런의 '오디세이'에도 출연합니다.
아직 제목이 없는 이 영화는 26번째 본드 영화가 되며, '듄' 시리즈를 만든 드니 빌뇌브가 감독합니다. 또한 아마존 MGM 스튜디오가 창작 통제권을 가진 첫 본드 작품입니다. 아마존은 수십 년 동안 프랜차이즈를 이끌어 온 가문의 바버라 브로콜리와 마이클 G. 윌슨이 2025년 물러난 뒤 책임을 맡았습니다.
알고 계셨나요? 1962년 첫 본드 영화 이후 이 시리즈는 전 세계 극장에서 70억 달러가 넘는 수익을 올려, 영화 역사상 가장 성공한 시리즈 중 하나가 되었습니다.
이 결정은 팬들의 논쟁을 훨씬 넘어서는 의미가 있습니다. 본드는 엔터테인먼트 업계에서 가장 가치 있는 지식재산 중 하나이고, 아마존의 첫 주연 배우 선택은 앞으로 수년간 이 프랜차이즈를 어떻게 이끌어 갈지 보여 주는 강한 신호입니다.
정리하면, 로버트 패틴슨은 아마존의 통제 아래 만드는 첫 본드 영화인 드니 빌뇌브 감독 작품에서 새 007이 됩니다.

5.headline: Pattinson Lands the Licence: Amazon Era of 007 Begins
p: Good morning, and welcome to your morning news in English.
After years of feverish speculation and endless debate among fans, the most coveted role in cinema has finally been filled: Robert Pattinson is the next James Bond.

According to news reports, the franchise confirmed on Monday that the 40-year-old British actor will step into the shoes of Ian Fleming's suave secret agent, becoming the seventh performer to play 007 in the official series. He inherits the tuxedo from Daniel Craig, whose five-film tenure concluded with No Time to Die in 2021.

For Pattinson, the casting is the latest chapter in a striking reinvention. Catapulted to fame as a brooding vampire in the Twilight saga, he spent the following years deliberately gravitating toward edgier, more demanding projects. He has since donned the cape as Batman, is currently in production on another instalment, and features in Christopher Nolan's The Odyssey. Earlier this month, trade reports had indicated that he had screen-tested for the part, lending credence to rumors that had swirled around his name for some time.

The as-yet-untitled picture, the 26th instalment of the series, will be helmed by Denis Villeneuve, the Canadian director behind the acclaimed Dune films. It also marks a watershed for the franchise itself: it is the first Bond film made under the creative control of Amazon MGM Studios, which took the reins after longtime stewards Barbara Broccoli and Michael G. Wilson bowed out in 2025. The Broccoli family had shepherded the series since its earliest days.
Did you know? Since Dr. No premiered in 1962, the Bond films have grossed more than seven billion dollars worldwide, making the series one of the most lucrative in film history.

The stakes, then, are considerable. Bond is far more than a character; he is a cultural institution, and Amazon's choice of leading man offers the clearest signal yet of how it intends to steer one of entertainment's crown jewels. How audiences respond in the coming weeks will be watched closely.
To sum up, Robert Pattinson has been cast as the new 007 in a Villeneuve-directed film, ushering in the Amazon era of James Bond.
Thank you for listening.
tr: 좋은 아침입니다. 아침 영어 뉴스에 오신 것을 환영합니다.
수년간의 열띤 추측과 팬들 사이의 끝없는 논쟁 끝에, 영화계에서 가장 탐나는 배역이 마침내 주인을 찾았습니다. 로버트 패틴슨이 다음 제임스 본드입니다.
보도에 따르면, 본드 프랜차이즈는 월요일 40세의 영국 배우가 이언 플레밍이 만든 세련된 비밀 요원의 자리를 이어받아, 공식 시리즈에서 007을 연기하는 일곱 번째 배우가 된다고 확인했습니다. 그는 2021년 '노 타임 투 다이'로 다섯 편의 임기를 마친 대니얼 크레이그에게서 턱시도를 물려받습니다.

패틴슨에게 이번 캐스팅은 눈에 띄는 변신의 최신 장입니다. '트와일라잇' 시리즈의 우수에 찬 뱀파이어로 단숨에 유명해진 그는 이후 몇 년 동안 일부러 더 날카롭고 까다로운 작품을 찾아갔습니다. 그 뒤 배트맨의 망토를 둘렀고, 현재 후속편을 촬영 중이며, 크리스토퍼 놀런의 '오디세이'에도 출연합니다. 이달 초 업계 보도는 그가 이 배역의 스크린 테스트를 받았다고 전해, 한동안 그의 이름을 둘러싸고 돌던 소문에 신빙성을 더했습니다.

아직 제목이 정해지지 않은 시리즈 26번째 작품은 호평받은 '듄' 영화들의 캐나다 출신 감독 드니 빌뇌브가 연출합니다. 이는 프랜차이즈 자체에도 분수령이 됩니다. 오랜 관리자였던 바버라 브로콜리와 마이클 G. 윌슨이 2025년 물러난 뒤 주도권을 잡은 아마존 MGM 스튜디오가 창작 통제권을 가진 첫 본드 영화이기 때문입니다. 브로콜리 가문은 시리즈 초창기부터 이를 이끌어 왔습니다.

정리하면, 로버트 패틴슨이 빌뇌브 감독 영화의 새 007로 캐스팅되며 제임스 본드의 아마존 시대가 열렸습니다.
들어 주셔서 감사합니다.

1.headline: More Foreign Students in Seoul Need Homes
p: Good morning. This is your morning news in English.
Where do foreign students in Seoul live? Many need a home.

Many students from other countries study in Seoul. There are about 62,900 of them. The number grows every year. But school dorms are small. Only about 6,700 students can live there. So many students look for rooms in the city.
In Korea, renters often pay a big deposit first. This is hard for students from other countries.
Now, big global companies want to offer homes for these students. They see a chance to make money. Some people worry that rent may go up.
Again, more foreign students are coming to Seoul. Big companies want to offer homes for them.
Thank you for listening.
tr: 좋은 아침입니다. 아침 영어 뉴스입니다.
서울의 외국인 학생들은 어디에서 살까요? 많은 학생이 집이 필요합니다.
다른 나라에서 온 많은 학생이 서울에서 공부합니다. 약 6만 2,900명입니다. 그 수는 해마다 늘고 있습니다. 하지만 학교 기숙사는 작습니다. 약 6,700명만 그곳에 살 수 있습니다. 그래서 많은 학생이 도시에서 방을 찾습니다.
한국에서는 세입자가 보통 큰 보증금을 먼저 냅니다. 이것은 다른 나라에서 온 학생들에게 어렵습니다.
이제 큰 글로벌 회사들이 이 학생들에게 집을 제공하고 싶어 합니다. 그들은 돈을 벌 기회를 봅니다. 어떤 사람들은 월세가 오를까 걱정합니다.
다시 말해, 더 많은 외국인 학생이 서울에 오고 있습니다. 큰 회사들이 그들에게 집을 제공하고 싶어 합니다.

2.headline: Foreign Student Boom Draws Global Investors to Seoul Housing
p: Good morning. This is your morning news in English.
More and more foreign students are coming to Seoul. But where do they live?

According to The Korea Herald, about 62,900 international students were studying at universities in Seoul as of April. The number of foreign undergraduate students went up about 11 percent in one year. But school dorms have room for only about 6,700 of them. So around 56,000 students must find a place to live in the city.
In Korea, renters usually pay a large deposit at the start. A deposit is money you pay first and get back later. This is difficult for many students from abroad.

Now, big global investment companies, like Morgan Stanley and Nuveen, are interested in student housing in Seoul. These are buildings just for students. An expert said these rooms can cost more each month, but they need a smaller deposit.

Why does this matter? Korea is becoming more popular with Asian students. One reason is stricter visa rules in the United States and the United Kingdom. But some people worry that big companies may make housing more expensive.
To sum up, the growing number of foreign students is making Seoul housing interesting to global investors.
Thank you for listening.

한국에서는 세입자가 보통 처음에 큰 보증금을 냅니다. 보증금은 먼저 냈다가 나중에 돌려받는 돈입니다. 이것은 해외에서 온 많은 학생에게 어렵습니다.
이제 모건스탠리와 누빈 같은 큰 글로벌 투자 회사들이 서울의 학생 주택에 관심을 보이고 있습니다. 학생만을 위한 건물입니다. 한 전문가는 이런 방은 매달 비용이 더 들 수 있지만 보증금은 더 적다고 말했습니다.
왜 중요할까요? 한국은 아시아 학생들에게 점점 인기를 얻고 있습니다. 한 가지 이유는 미국과 영국의 더 엄격해진 비자 규정입니다. 하지만 어떤 사람들은 큰 회사들이 집값을 더 비싸게 만들까 걱정합니다.
정리하면, 늘어나는 외국인 학생 때문에 글로벌 투자자들이 서울 주택에 관심을 갖게 되었습니다.

The number of foreign undergraduate students rose about 11 percent in one year. But university dormitories have room for only about 6,700 of them. That means roughly 56,000 students must find homes in the private rental market.

Now, large global investment firms such as Invesco, Hines, Morgan Stanley and Nuveen are looking at this market, the report says. Thank you for listening.

4.headline: Foreign Student Surge Puts Seoul Housing on Global Investors' Radar
p: Good morning, and welcome to your morning news in English.
Seoul's universities are attracting more international students than ever, and that boom is turning student housing into a target for some of the world's biggest property investors.

According to The Korea Herald, about 62,900 international students were enrolled in degree programs at Seoul universities as of April 2026, with foreign undergraduate enrollment up around 11 percent from a year earlier. University dormitories, however, house only an estimated 6,700 of them. That leaves roughly 56,000 students competing for rooms in the city's private rental market.

For many of them, the biggest obstacle is money up front. Korean landlords typically demand large deposits, and the country's jeonse system can require a lump sum worth a large share of a home's value. Students arriving from abroad often struggle to raise such amounts.

Global investors see an opportunity. The report says firms including Invesco, Hines, Morgan Stanley and Nuveen are eyeing the market for purpose-built student housing. Josh Rose-Nokes, who leads Asia Pacific living research at the real estate services firm Cushman and Wakefield, said studio-style, all-inclusive units with lower deposits can charge rents roughly 20 percent above traditional properties, while students' total yearly housing costs stay about the same.

Demand is expected to remain strong. Rose-Nokes noted that tighter visa rules in the United States and the United Kingdom are steering Asian students toward Korea. Still, the arrival of large institutional landlords raises affordability concerns in a country that is highly sensitive to corporate involvement in housing. He said investors would need to show they are adding new supply rather than simply buying existing homes.
To sum up, a surge in foreign students has created a housing gap in Seoul, and global investors are moving to fill it, though questions about affordability remain.
Thank you for listening.

5.headline: Seoul's International Student Boom Lures Global Capital into Campus Housing
p: Good morning, and welcome to your morning news in English.
A quiet demographic shift on Seoul's campuses is catching the eye of some of the biggest names in global real estate.

According to The Korea Herald, roughly 62,900 international students were pursuing degrees at universities in the capital as of April 2026, with foreign undergraduate enrollment climbing by about 11 percent year on year. University dormitories, however, accommodate an estimated 6,700 of them, leaving some 56,000 to fend for themselves in an already tight private rental market. Korea has for years courted overseas students, partly to offset a shrinking pool of domestic applicants as its birth rate falls.

For many, the sticking point is the upfront outlay. Korean leases typically hinge on hefty deposits, and the distinctive jeonse system can demand a lump sum equivalent to a substantial share of a property's value, a prohibitive hurdle for many newcomers from abroad. Even monthly rental arrangements, the main alternative, usually come with a sizable deposit.

That mismatch has not gone unnoticed. The report names Invesco, Hines, Morgan Stanley and Nuveen among the institutional players sizing up purpose-built student accommodation. Josh Rose-Nokes, head of Asia Pacific living research at the property consultancy Cushman and Wakefield, said studio-style, all-inclusive units with lower deposits can command rents about 20 percent higher than conventional properties while keeping tenants' annual outlay broadly comparable. He suggested that institutional owners could tie their returns to occupancy levels and the quality of their services.

The tailwinds look durable. Rose-Nokes pointed to tighter visa regimes in the United States and Britain as a factor nudging Asian students toward Korea. Yet the arrival of deep-pocketed landlords is bound to stir unease in a country where corporate involvement in housing is a notoriously sensitive issue. To win public acceptance, he argued, investors will have to demonstrate that they are adding to the housing stock rather than merely snapping up existing homes, and clearer regulatory standards would help.

To sum up, Seoul's international student boom has opened up a sizable housing gap, and global capital is lining up to fill it, though the question of who ultimately bears the cost is far from settled.
Thank you for listening.
